item.title: Large language model agents in watershed environmental response: a hypothesis-and-theory framework for the cognitive orchestration layer
item.description: Introduction Watershed environmental governance increasingly combines dense sensing infrastructure with institutions whose attention, authority, and coordination capacity remain limited. We develop the cognitive orchestration layer as a theory-building concept for examining how large language model (LLM)-based agents may connect sensing, assessment, decision advice, institutional response, and feedback without displacing domain models or public authority. item.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) promise to accelerate discovery by reasoning across the ever-expanding landscape of scientific knowledge. item.title: Authorization assurance for tool-using LLM agents: a structured review of enforcement semantics and effect-level security evidence
item.description: Abstract Tool-using large language model (LLM) agents exercise authority over protected resources through APIs, tools, credentials, and external services. This structured review asks whether authorization claims are supported at the enforcement and observation boundaries relevant to the claimed effect. item.title: When Does Hallucination Propagate? Reconciling Six Formalizations of Error Spread in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
item.description: Abstract Multi-agent LLM systems are deployed on the assumption that agents checking one another reduce hallucination. Two studies of the same linear topology contradict it in opposite directions, and both are right: one measures prevalence, the other detectability, and a claim can become rarer and less visible at once. item.title: Phygital research fit: toward a theory-building framework for transformative and sustainable service research
item.description: Phygital service research requires evidence of how physical and digital elements jointly produce service outcomes. We develop phygital research fit as alignment among the phenomenon, theory, evidence, research design, and validity and ethical criteria. item.description: Abstract* Background Adaptive generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used to personalize learning, yet evidence remains fragmented across system design, human–AI co-regulation, self-regulated learning (SRL), sustained behavioral outcomes, and ethics. item.title: Nursing roles and tasks in transitional care for young people with chronic conditions: An integrative review
item.description: BACKGROUND: Nurses play a pivotal role in supporting adolescents with somatic chronic conditions during transition to adult care, yet their specific contributions within multidisciplinary teams remain insufficiently defined and are often overlooked. OBJECTIVE: To synthesize the nursing roles and tasks during the transition of adolescents with chronic conditions from pediatric to adult hospital services. item.description: Agents are increasingly deployed with real autonomy in web application and network penetration testing, where a single out-of-scope action can breach a client’s engagement boundary. item.title: A Governed Computational Architecture for Predictive Process Monitoring with Policy-Constrained Orchestration and Auditable Decision Making
item.description: Abstract Predictive process monitoring enables organizations to anticipate process outcomes from event logs, although deployment in real operational environments remains challenging due to temporal drift, heterogeneous traces, and limited interpretability of deep predictive models. item.title: Evaluating AI Alignment in LLMs: Output Analysis of Value Priorities Across 75 Models with Human Benchmarking
item.description: Large language models (LLMs) shape human–AI interaction, yet capability and safety benchmarks provide limited insight into their expressed value priorities. Across three studies, we developed an output-based approach to evaluating correspondence between LLM priorities and human judgements of optimal AI functioning. item.description: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. item.description: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. item.title: Can TDD improve the quality of LLM-migrated code? : A pilot study in an industrial context
item.description: The emergence of Large Language Models (LLM) has created new possibilities for automating software development, yet ensuring the quality of AI-generated code remains a major challenge. We aim to investigate if Test-Driven Development (TDD) can improve the quality of code generated by an LLM in a fully autonomous context, within a pilot project at Decerno AB. item.title: From Coding to Creativity: Integrating Design Thinking into IT and Technology Education
item.description: This study examines how the integration of Design Thinking into Information Technology (IT) and technology education can bridge technical programming skills and creative, human-centered problem-solving.
